revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Surveillance Van Budget
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Reyes can spend at most $85 on gas for her surveillance van this week. She has already spent $52. Write an inequality for the additional amount g she can still spend, solve it, and describe how you would graph the solution set on a number line.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The inequality is 52 + g ≤ 85. Subtracting 52 from both sides: g ≤ 85 − 52 = 33. Since ≤ includes the boundary, the graph has a closed circle at 33, shaded to the left (toward smaller values), showing that Detective Reyes can spend $33 or less on additional gas this week.

questions.explanation: Subtract 6 from both sides: x > 14 − 6 = 8. Graph: open circle at 8, shade right.
choiceFeedback: The boundary number is right, but the inequality symbol flipped. Adding or subtracting on both sides never changes the direction of the symbol.
An inequality has many solutions, not just one. Look at what the > symbol allows on either side of the boundary.
Not quite. Subtract 6 from both sides: x > 14 − 6 = ___.
hints: Solve it like an equation: x has 6 added to it. The > symbol just rides along.
Subtract 6 from both sides — the inequality symbol keeps pointing the same way when you subtract.
Compute 14 − 6 and keep the >. Then test: pick a number bigger than your result and check it makes x + 6 > 14 true.
questions.explanationEs: Resta 6 en ambos lados: x > 14 − 6 = 8. Gráfica: círculo abierto en 8, sombrea hacia la derecha.
hintsEs: Resuélvelo como una ecuación: a x se le suman 6. El símbolo > solo va de acompañante.
Resta 6 de ambos lados: el símbolo de desigualdad sigue apuntando igual cuando restas.
Calcula 14 − 6 y conserva el >. Luego prueba: escoge un número mayor que tu resultado y revisa que haga verdadera x + 6 > 14.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Solve and Graph Inequalities is shading the number line in the wrong direction after solving. For example, a student solves x + 4 > 10 correctly to get x > 6, but then shades LEFT toward smaller numbers instead of RIGHT toward greater numbers. The shading direction always matches the solved symbol, not the original problem: '>' and '≥' shade right (greater numbers), '<' and '≤' shade left (smaller numbers) — check this AFTER you solve, not before. To catch this mistake, substitute one shaded value and one unshaded value back into the original inequality: the shaded value should make it true, and the unshaded value should make it false.

level2.stem: Is x = 5 a solution to x + 4 > 12?
choices: No, because 5 + 4 = 9, and 9 is not greater than 12
level2.explanation: Substitute: 5 + 4 = 9. Since 9 > 12 is false, x = 5 is NOT a solution.
choiceFeedback: Your arithmetic is right, but then compare: is 9 actually greater than 12?
Comparing 5 with the 4 in the expression skips the actual test. Substitute 5 for x, simplify the left side, then compare that result with 12.
Comparing x directly with 12 leaves out the + 4. Substitute first, then compare the simplified left side with 12.
hints: 'Is 5 a solution?' means: substitute 5 for x and see whether the statement comes out TRUE.
Replace x with 5 and compute the left side completely. Then compare that result to 12 honestly — is it really greater?
Compute 5 + 4 first. Then ask: is that total greater than 12? Your yes-or-no needs the correct REASON attached to it.
level2.explanationEs: Sustituye: 5 + 4 = 9. Como 9 > 12 es falso, x = 5 NO es una solución.
choicesEs: No, porque 5 + 4 = 9, y 9 no es mayor que 12
hintsEs: '¿Es 5 una solución?' significa: sustituye 5 por x y ve si el enunciado resulta VERDADERO.
Reemplaza x por 5 y calcula el lado izquierdo completo. Luego compara ese resultado con 12 con honestidad: ¿de verdad es mayor?
Calcula primero 5 + 4. Luego pregunta: ¿ese total es mayor que 12? Tu sí o no necesita llevar la RAZÓN correcta.

level2.explanation: A solution makes x > 7 true. Substitute each: 9 > 7 is true, but 7 > 7, 5 > 7, and 3 > 7 are all false. So 9 is the solution that opens the gate.
choiceFeedback: 3 > 7 is not a true statement, so 3 cannot be in the solution set. Test each value by putting it into the inequality.
Substituting gives 5 > 7, which is false. Look for a value that lands on the greater side of 7.
Not quite. A solution makes x > 7 true.
level2.stemEs: Pista 1: ¿cuál valor es una solución de x > 7?
level2.explanationEs: Una solución hace verdadera la desigualdad x > 7. Sustituye cada uno: 9 > 7 es verdadero, pero 7 > 7, 5 > 7 y 3 > 7 son todos falsos. Por eso 9 es la solución que abre la puerta.
hints: A solution is any value that makes the inequality a true statement.
Substitute each choice for x and decide whether the statement it creates is true.
Start at the bottom of the list: replace x with 3 and check whether 3 > 7 is true. Work up through the choices the same way.
hintsEs: Una solución es cualquier valor que hace verdadero el enunciado de la desigualdad.
Sustituye cada opción en lugar de x y decide si el enunciado que se forma es verdadero.
Empieza por el final de la lista: reemplaza x por 3 y comprueba si 3 > 7 es verdadero. Sigue subiendo por las opciones de la misma manera.

level2.stem: Clue 2: Is 5 a solution of x ≤ 5?
choices: No, because 5 is not less than 5
No, because ≤ means only smaller numbers
Yes, but only because 5 is odd
level2.explanation: Substitute x = 5 into x ≤ 5. That gives 5 ≤ 5. The symbol ≤ means ‘less than OR equal to,’ so this is true. The boundary value 5 IS a solution, so the gate opens.
choiceFeedback: True, 5 is not less than 5 — but ≤ also allows equal to.
The ≤ symbol covers more than "smaller" — read the second half of its name, then re-test the boundary value.
Whether a number is odd or even has nothing to do with inequalities. Substitute the value and check the symbol instead.
level2.explanationEs: Sustituye x = 5 en x ≤ 5. Eso da 5 ≤ 5. El símbolo ≤ significa ‘menor que O igual a’, así que es verdadero. El valor límite 5 SÍ es una solución, así que la puerta se abre.
hints: The symbol ≤ is read "less than or equal to" — it has two ways of being satisfied.
Substitute 5 for x and check whether either part of that symbol is satisfied.
The statement becomes 5 ≤ 5. Ask yourself whether the "or equal to" half of the symbol is met.
hintsEs: El símbolo ≤ se lee "menor que o igual a": tiene dos maneras de cumplirse.
Sustituye 5 en lugar de x y comprueba si se cumple alguna de las dos partes de ese símbolo.
El enunciado queda 5 ≤ 5. Pregúntate si se cumple la parte de "o igual a" del símbolo.
choicesEs: No, porque 5 no es menor que 5
No, porque ≤ significa solo números más pequeños
Sí, pero solo porque 5 es impar

level2.stem: Final gate — describe the solution set. The vault rule is x > 7. What does the solution set mean?
choices: All numbers greater than 7, like 8, 9, 10, … (but NOT 7 itself)
level2.explanation: The solution set is every value that makes x > 7 true. That means all numbers greater than 7, such as 8, 9, 10, and beyond. Because > does not include the boundary, 7 itself is NOT in the solution set.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. The solution set is every value that makes x > 7 true.
The > symbol points toward values above 7, not below it. Substitute a number smaller than 7 and see whether it works.
Not every number works — try substituting 7 and then a value below it, and check whether the statement stays true.
level2.stemEs: Puerta final: describe el conjunto solución. La regla de la bóveda es x > 7. ¿Qué significa el conjunto solución?
level2.explanationEs: El conjunto solución es todo valor que hace verdadera la desigualdad x > 7. Eso significa todos los números mayores que 7, como 8, 9, 10 y más. Como > no incluye el valor límite, el 7 NO está en el conjunto solución.
hints: A solution set is every value that makes the inequality true, not just one number.
Decide two things: which side of 7 the values fall on, and whether 7 itself counts.
Test x = 7 in x > 7 and see whether the statement is true — that tells you whether the boundary belongs in the set.
hintsEs: Un conjunto solución es todo valor que hace verdadera la desigualdad, no solo un número.
Decide dos cosas: de qué lado del 7 están los valores y si el 7 mismo cuenta.
Prueba x = 7 en x > 7 y observa si el enunciado es verdadero; eso te dice si el valor límite pertenece al conjunto.
choicesEs: Todos los números mayores que 7, como 8, 9, 10, … (pero NO el 7 mismo)

level2.prompt: A detective has a budget of at most $100 for supplies. She already spent $37 on gloves. Write an inequality for the remaining amount r she can spend, solve it, graph it, and name three possible values for r.
level2.sentenceFrame: Inequality: 37 + r ≤ ___. Solving: r ≤ ___ − 37 = ___. Graph: ___ circle at ___, shade ___. Three possible values: ___.
level2.hint: Use a strategy or example from the lesson to help you explain your answer.
hints: 'At most $100' caps the TOTAL: the $37 already spent plus the remaining amount r must stay within 100.
Model it as 37 + r ≤ 100, then subtract 37 from both sides. 'At most' means the boundary IS allowed — remember that for the circle.
Compute 100 − 37 to find r's boundary. Then choose any three amounts at or below that boundary as your example values.
level2.explanation: "At most $100" puts a cap on the total, so the model is 37 + r ≤ 100. Subtracting 37 from both sides gives r ≤ 63. Because "at most" allows the boundary itself, the graph is a closed circle at 63 shaded to the left, and amounts such as $63, $40, and $10 are all possible values of r.
level2.explanationEs: "Como máximo $100" pone un tope al total, así que el modelo es 37 + r ≤ 100. Al restar 37 en ambos lados: r ≤ 63. Como "como máximo" permite el propio valor límite, la gráfica lleva un círculo cerrado en 63 sombreado hacia la izquierda, y cantidades como $63, $40 y $10 son valores posibles de r.
level2.promptEs: Una detective tiene un presupuesto de a lo más $100 para materiales. Ya gastó $37 en guantes. Escribe una desigualdad para la cantidad restante r que puede gastar, resuélvela, grafícala y nombra tres valores posibles de r.
hintsEs: 'A lo sumo $100' limita el TOTAL: los $37 ya gastados más la cantidad restante r deben quedarse dentro de 100.
Modélalo como 37 + r ≤ 100 y luego resta 37 de ambos lados. 'A lo sumo' significa que el límite SÍ se permite; recuérdalo para el círculo.
Calcula 100 − 37 para hallar el límite de r. Luego escoge tres cantidades iguales o menores que ese límite como tus valores de ejemplo.

tool.instructions: These are the SOLUTION graphs for the inequalities you just solved. Write the solution each graph shows.
hints: Solving an inequality works like solving an equation: undo the operation on both sides.
The symbol you started with is the symbol you graph — > and < get an open circle, ≥ and ≤ get a closed one.
